summary: Private-Wi-Fi HTTPS LAN mode implemented with one project-local Bun TLS entry bound only to 192.168.1.98:8443, serving the same-origin LAN web build and proxying /api, /health, /ready and WebSocket upgrades to the existing native Mode A API authority on 127.0.0.1:3000 (same PostgreSQL). LAN-01/03/04/05/06/07 verified with real HTTPS API/DB/native-WS evidence and both-mode regression (Mode A 91/0, Mode B Docker runner 91/0). LAN-02 (physical iPhone Safari with user-installed trusted CA) is NOT RUN and BLOCKED_PENDING_USER_ACTION: certificate profile installation/trust on the iPhone is an explicit user action. No public tunnel, DB exposure, global install, firewall/router/system trust change, TLS bypass or HTTP downgrade; keys stay ignored and private. C1 remains PARTIAL with C1-EG-01/02 unchanged.
topology: Bun TLS entry on private LAN IP -> static LAN web build + same-origin proxy for /api,/health,/ready,/ws -> existing native Mode A API 127.0.0.1:3000 -> PostgreSQL 127.0.0.1:5433
pending_user_actions: Confirm the iPhone is on the same private Wi-Fi as 192.168.1.98 (not guest/isolated; no VPN conflict)
Transfer only the public CA certificate .local/lan-certs/ca.crt to the iPhone (never ca.key/server.key)
Install the certificate profile on the iPhone (Settings > General > VPN & Device Management)
Enable SSL trust for the development CA (Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings)
Allow the Bun listener if macOS prompts for incoming connections (user firewall decision)
Open https://192.168.1.98:8443/join in Safari with ROOM-01 and record the actual iPhone model/iOS/Safari results
Remove the development CA profile after testing
